# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-vultisig/blob/cb72b1e9053c02a58d874ff376359a83dc3f0742/src/ILOManager.sol#L57-L65
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-vultisig/blob/cb72b1e9053c02a58d874ff376359a83dc3f0742/src/ILOManager.sol#L187-L198


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
New project which also creates a new uniswap pool could fail to launch due to the assumption that the price in uniswap's pool slot0 will remain same from the creation time of project to the launch time. 

As uniswap pool is a public pool, price could change due to interactions leading to failure to launch of the project due to the below check at the time of launch.

As the launch has potential to fail, the claim is also not possible leading to locking of user funds.

```
 require(_cachedProject[uniV3PoolAddress].initialPoolPriceX96 == sqrtPriceX96, "UV3P");

```
The above check assumes that the configured price at the time of launch and price returned by the uniswap pool will remain the same, which is an incorrect assumption.

## Proof of Concept
Anyone can initialize a project by calling initProject() function. As part of the initialization, the logic checks for existence of the pool in Uniswap factory and if not, creates a new pool in uniswap
and sets the initial sqrt price for the pool. One of the key parameter passed during the project creation is the launchTime which defines when the launch for the project can happen and when can the refund for the
pools under the project can be claimed.

All the key parameters are stored in the contract in _cachedProject mapping.

```
    function _initUniV3PoolIfNecessary(PoolAddress.PoolKey memory poolKey, uint160 sqrtPriceX96) internal returns (address pool) {
        pool = IUniswapV3Factory(UNIV3_FACTORY).getPool(poolKey.token0, poolKey.token1, poolKey.fee);
        if (pool == address(0)) {
            pool = IUniswapV3Factory(UNIV3_FACTORY).createPool(poolKey.token0, poolKey.token1, poolKey.fee);
            IUniswapV3Pool(pool).initialize(sqrtPriceX96);
        }

```
The owner can then start adding pools using initILOPool() function.

At the time of launch, one of the key conditions being checked is if the configured price is equal to 
Uniswap pool's slot 0 price. Incase the price does not match, the launch function will essentially revert.

Uniswap pool is a public accessible pool and any one should be able to interact with the Uniswap pool and  move the price for the pair directly impacting the slot0 price.

This will lead to failure of launch of the project.

```
 function launch(address uniV3PoolAddress) external override {
        require(block.timestamp > _cachedProject[uniV3PoolAddress].launchTime, "LT");
        (uint160 sqrtPriceX96, , , , , , ) = IUniswapV3Pool(uniV3PoolAddress).slot0();
 ===>   require(_cachedProject[uniV3PoolAddress].initialPoolPriceX96 == sqrtPriceX96, "UV3P");// audit
        ... 
    }
```
There is a time window between when the project was created and when it will be launched. The time difference leaves a natural opportunity for any one to interact with the newly created pool in uni-swap causing the price to shift in this mean time.

The change is price can be intentional by a bad actor front running the launch call or natural change in price as part of participation by external parties. 


## Tools Used
Manual review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
The assumption that price will remain same from creation of the project in the local contract storage and in Uni-swap pool is an incorrect assumption and hence the check should be removed. As public pool, the price has natural scope to move.








## Assessed type

Uniswap

# Lines of code

# Vulnerability details

## Impact
The contract of `Vultisig` does not have any protection against the well-known “Multiple Withdrawal Attack” attack on the `approve` method of the `ERC20` standard.
Although this attack poses a limited risk in specific situations, it is worth mentioning to consider it for possible future operations.

## Proof of Concept
```solidity
function approveAndCall(address spender, uint256 amount, bytes calldata extraData) external returns (bool) {
        // Approve the spender to spend the tokens
>>      _approve(msg.sender, spender, amount); // @audit-issue can be frontrun

        // Call the receiveApproval function on the spender contract
        IApproveAndCallReceiver(spender).receiveApproval(msg.sender, amount, address(this), extraData); //! address(this) used as token

        return true;
    }
```
An approved `spender` may fron-run the `owner` and transfer the originally approved `amount` before the `owner` changes it to a new value and then transfer the new `amount` too.

## Tools Used
Manual Review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
There are solutions to mitigate this front running such as:
1. first reduce the `spender's allowance to 0` and set the desired value 
2. another solution could be the one that `OpenZeppelin` offers, where the non-standard `decreaseAllowance()` and `increaseAllowance()` functions have been added to mitigate the well-known issues involving setting allowances.

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-vultisig/blob/cb72b1e9053c02a58d874ff376359a83dc3f0742/src/ILOManager.sol#L76-L77


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
The absence of a validation check to ensure that the `params.end` timestamp is in the `future` can lead to immediate sale expiration of the ILO pool upon initialization. This means that no sales will be possible as the `endTime` would have already passed.

## Vulnerability Details
The [initILOPool()](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-vultisig/blob/cb72b1e9053c02a58d874ff376359a83dc3f0742/src/ILOManager.sol#L76-L77) function is designed to initialize an  (ILO) pool with specific parameters provided by the project admin. These parameters include the `start` and `end` times for the sale.

The function performs several checks to ensure the validity of these parameters, such as verifying that the `start time` is before the `end time` and that the `end time` is before the project's `launch time`. 
```solidity
// validate time for sale start and end compared to launch time
require(params.start < params.end && params.end < _project.launchTime, "PT");
```
However, it lacks a crucial validation step to ensure that the `endTime` is in the future relative to the current timestamp.

The absence of a check to confirm that `params.end` is in the future can lead to significant issues. Specifically, if the `endTime` is set to a timestamp that has already passed,  the sale period  within the pool  will be considered expired immediately upon initialization. 

**Consider the requirement in the [buy()](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-vultisig/blob/cb72b1e9053c02a58d874ff376359a83dc3f0742/src/ILOPool.sol#L134) function**.
```solidity
require(block.timestamp > saleInfo.start && block.timestamp < saleInfo.end, "ST");
```
As seen, for a `buy` trade to be executed, `block.timestamp` must be less than `saleInfo.end`

---> If `params.end` is set to a timestamp before the current `block.timestamp`, the pool will close immediately, preventing any sales. This means that no participants will be able to contribute to the `sale`, rendering the pool ineffective for its intended purpose.

## Tools Used
Manual Review

## Recommended mitigation steps
The `initILOPool()` function should ensure that the `params.end` is in the future relative to the current timestamp.
```diff
    // validate time for sale start and end compared to launch time
    require(params.start < params.end && params.end < _project.launchTime, "PT");
+   require(params.end > block.timestamp, "End time must be in the future");
```








## Assessed type

Invalid Validation

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-vultisig/blob/cb72b1e9053c02a58d874ff376359a83dc3f0742/src/ILOManager.sol#L191-L195

# Vulnerability details

## Impact
The `initILOPool()` function creates an `iloPoolAddress` and appends it to the `_initializedILOPools[params.uniV3Pool]` array. When the `launch()` and `claimRefund()` functions are called, they loop through the entire `_initializedILOPools[params.uniV3Pool]` array to launch each pool and claim project refund for each pool respectively. 

If this array grows too large, the gas required to iterate over the array and launch each pool or claim project refund for each pool may exceed the block gas limit causing the transaction to fail.

## Vulnerability Details
As more `ILO` pools are initialized in [initILOPool()](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-vultisig/blob/cb72b1e9053c02a58d874ff376359a83dc3f0742/src/ILOManager.sol#L106), the `_initializedILOPools[params.uniV3Pool]` array grows in size. Each new pool added increases the length of the array.
```solidity
    bytes32 salt = keccak256(abi.encodePacked(
        ChainId.get(),
        params.uniV3Pool,
        _initializedILOPools[params.uniV3Pool].length
    ));
    iloPoolAddress = Clones.cloneDeterministic(ILO_POOL_IMPLEMENTATION, salt); // @audit Pool created
    //...
    _initializedILOPools[params.uniV3Pool].push(iloPoolAddress); //@audit Array grows
```
The [launch()](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-vultisig/blob/cb72b1e9053c02a58d874ff376359a83dc3f0742/src/ILOManager.sol#L191-L195) function then iterates over the entire `_initializedILOPools[params.uniV3Pool]` array.
For each pool in the array, it calls the `launch()` method on the `ILOPool` contract.
```solidity
    address[] memory initializedPools = _initializedILOPools[uniV3PoolAddress];
    require(initializedPools.length > 0, "NP");
    for (uint256 i = 0; i < initializedPools.length; i++) { // @audit Loop entire array and launch each one
        IILOPool(initializedPools[i]).launch();
    }
```
The [claimRefund()](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-vultisig/blob/cb72b1e9053c02a58d874ff376359a83dc3f0742/src/ILOManager.sol#L203-L206) function also iterates over the entire `_initializedILOPools[params.uniV3Pool]` array.
```solidity
        address[] memory initializedPools = _initializedILOPools[uniV3PoolAddress];
        for (uint256 i = 0; i < initializedPools.length; i++) { // @audit Full iteration
            totalRefundAmount += IILOPool(initializedPools[i]).claimProjectRefund(_cachedProject[uniV3PoolAddress].admin);
        }
```

As the array grows, the number of iterations in the loop increases. Each iteration consumes gas, and the total gas required can exceed the block gas limit if the array is too large. This can lead to an Out-of-Gas (OOG) error, causing the transaction to revert.

## Tools Used
Manual Review

## Recommended mitigation steps
Implement batch processing to launch pools/claim project refund in smaller, manageable groups. This reduces the number of iterations per transaction, lowering the gas consumption.











## Assessed type

DoS

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-vultisig/blob/7fb0da757c98116090f35810146ea742ca3b94da/hardhat-vultisig/contracts/oracles/uniswap/uniswapv0.8/FullMath.sol#L14


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
`Uniswap` math libraries rely on wrapping behavior for conducting arithmetic operations. Solidity version `0.8.0` introduced checked arithmetic by default where operations that cause an `overflow` would revert.

## Proof of Concept
The protocol uses FullMath library when fetching TWAP for 1 VULT for the last 30 mins via the [peek()](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-vultisig/blob/cb72b1e9053c02a58d874ff376359a83dc3f0742/hardhat-vultisig/contracts/oracles/uniswap/UniswapV3Oracle.sol#L38-L46) function:
```solidity
/// @notice Returns TWAP price for 1 VULT for the last 30 mins
    function peek(uint256 baseAmount) external view returns (uint256) {
        uint32 longestPeriod = OracleLibrary.getOldestObservationSecondsAgo(pool);
        uint32 period = PERIOD < longestPeriod ? PERIOD : longestPeriod;
        int24 tick = OracleLibrary.consult(pool, period);
>>      uint256 quotedWETHAmount = OracleLibrary.getQuoteAtTick(tick, BASE_AMOUNT, baseToken, WETH); // @audit-issue FullMath may overflow
        // Apply 5% slippage
        return (quotedWETHAmount * baseAmount * 95) / 1e20; // 100 / 1e18
    }
```
This is then used to calculate rough ETH amount for VULT amount in [checkWhitelist()](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-vultisig/blob/cb72b1e9053c02a58d874ff376359a83dc3f0742/hardhat-vultisig/contracts/Whitelist.sol#L220-L221):
```solidity
      // Calculate rough ETH amount for VULT amount
>>    uint256 estimatedETHAmount = IOracle(_oracle).peek(amount);
```
All these calculation may overflow and break the sytem where they are needed.

Since the code was adapted from `Uniswap` and written in Solidity version `0.4.0`, these arithmetic operations should be wrapped in an `unchecked` block.

## Tools Used
Manual Review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Add an `unchecked` block to the following functions in `TickMath.sol` and `FullMath.sol`.
- `mulDiv()`
- `mulDivRoundingUp()`
- `getSqrtRatioAtTick()`
- `getTickAtSqrtRatio()`





## Assessed type

Uniswap

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-vultisig/blob/cb72b1e9053c02a58d874ff376359a83dc3f0742/hardhat-vultisig/contracts/Whitelist.sol#L29
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-vultisig/blob/main/hardhat-vultisig/contracts/Whitelist.sol#L65-L74


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
Based on `_isSelfWhitelistDisabled` value, either anyone can whitelist himself or only the owner can whitelist users. However on deploy this value by default is `false`, which means that anyone can whitelist himself.

## Proof of Concept
In Solidity, by default boolean values are set to `false`. The `_isSelfWhitelistDisabled` variable is used as flag and can be changed by the owner by calling `setIsSelfWhitelistDisabled` function. If we take a look at the `receive` function:

```solidity
    receive() external payable {
        if (_isSelfWhitelistDisabled) { // @audit false by default
            revert SelfWhitelistDisabled();
        }
        if (_isBlacklisted[_msgSender()]) { // @audit false by default
            revert Blacklisted();
        }
        _addWhitelistedAddress(_msgSender());
        payable(_msgSender()).transfer(msg.value);
    }
```

We can see that the checks will pass as they are not configured yet. This means that anyone can call `receive` only paying the gas fees and be whitelisted. Later on owner can change the flag, but not notice that there are addresses that are whitelisted.

## Tools Used
Manual Review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Either set the flag to `true` in the constructor or add parameter to constructor that will allow owners to choose the flag's value.


## Assessed type

Access Control

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-vultisig/blob/main/src/base/PeripheryPayments.sol#L30


# Vulnerability details


## Impact
The project uses `transfer()` for sending ETH to the caller after determining the payout amount.

```javascript
IWETH9(WETH9).transfer(recipient, value);
```

However, use of `transfer()` has the risk that it will not work if the gas cost increases/decrease. The assumption that gas cost stays fixed no longer holds true since Istanbul hard fork. see https://swcregistry.io/docs/SWC-134/. When that happens, it will prevent the caller from receiving ETH payout.


## Proof of Concept

In the past `transfer()` was recommended to prevent re-entrancy attacks (i.e. via receive/fallback) as it limits forwarded gas to 2300. Now the security recommendation to prevent re-entrancy is to ensure Check-Effects-Interactions Pattern or use a Reentrancy guard.

The transfer method is used to send ether to a recipient. It is generally considered unsafe because it forwards a fixed amount of 2300 gas, which might not be enough for certain operations in the recipient's fallback or receive function. If the recipient is a contract that requires more than 2300 gas, the transaction will revert.

## Tools Used
Manual review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Instead of using `transfer`, it is recommended to use `call` to send ether, which allows specifying the amount of gas to forward. 


## Assessed type

ETH-Transfer

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-vultisig/blob/cb72b1e9053c02a58d874ff376359a83dc3f0742/hardhat-vultisig/contracts/oracles/uniswap/UniswapV3Oracle.sol#L45


# Vulnerability details

## Root of the Bug
The bug is arises from the incorrect operation when applying the 5% slippage in the peek function. the formula used for slippage id  divides the calculated amount by an incorrect factor (1e20), and this  leading to unintended precision loss and inaccurate results.
Here : 

```solidity
return (quotedWETHAmount * baseAmount * 95) / 1e20; // Incorrect division factor
```

The formula attempts to apply a 5% reduction by multiplying by 95 and then dividing by 1e20, and  the divisor 1e20 is incorrect for handling both the precision adjustment (typically 1e18 for 18 decimals) and the percentage reduction. It introduces an additional precision loss beyond what is necessary, leading to an unintended reduction in the final quoted amount, and the quotedWETHAmount is multiplied by baseAmount to scale the quote according to the specified amount.
The result is then multiplied by 95 to apply the 5% reduction.

The intended adjustment should divide by 1e18 (for decimal precision) and then by 100 for the percentage factor.
The current code divides by 1e20, combining both precision and percentage adjustments but with an incorrect total factor, causing an overly large réduction

## Impact
The incorrect application of slippage can lead to inaccurate price quotes for 1 VULT, potentially resulting in financial discrepancies.


- here is an example show the bug : 

- We have this 
return (quotedWETHAmount * baseAmount * 95) / 1e20;

- The Calculation is :

Multiply by Base Amount:
WETH for 2 VULT=1×10(18) wei×2
=2×10(18) wei

Apply 5% Slippage:
Adjusted WETH=(2×10(18) wei×95)/1×10(20)

Calculate Result:
Adjusted WETH=(190×10(18))/
(1×10(20))=0.0019 wei

- The result, 0.0019 wei, is significantly lower than expected due to the incorrect division by 1e20.


## Tools Used
Manual review 
## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Need to update the division factor to correctly handle both precision and percentage adjustments



## Assessed type

Other

# Vulnerability details

## Impact
The `whenNotInitialized()` modifier is there to prevent the `ILOPool.sol` to get initialized again, essentially act as a constructor, and it does that  by cheking `initialized != true`
```java 
modifier whenNotInitialized() {
        require(!_initialized,"The contract is already Initialized");
        _;
        _initialized = true;
    }
```
 But since we are calling `_disableInitialize()` in he constructor
```java 
function _disableInitialize() internal {
        _initialized = true;
    }
``` 
`_initialized` will already be true , so we will not be able to call `initialize()`

warden_comment:
# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-vultisig/blob/cb72b1e9053c02a58d874ff376359a83dc3f0742/src/ILOPool.sol#L184
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-vultisig/blob/cb72b1e9053c02a58d874ff376359a83dc3f0742/src/ILOPool.sol#L350
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-vultisig/blob/cb72b1e9053c02a58d874ff376359a83dc3f0742/src/base/Multicall.sol#L11


# Vulnerability details

 
 


 
 [Multicall](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-vultisig/blob/cb72b1e9053c02a58d874ff376359a83dc3f0742/src/base/Multicall.sol) is a pattern to call several contract endpoints in one transaction, using `delegatecall`. A contract endpoint may implicitly assume that it is called in a single transaction, by looking at `msg.value`. Since the value is defined per transaction, calling the same endpoint twice in one `multicall` means that the same `msg.value` may be read several times, even though the value was only transferred once.

[ILOPool](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-vultisig/blob/cb72b1e9053c02a58d874ff376359a83dc3f0742/src/ILOPool.sol#) contract inherits from the [Multicall](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-vultisig/blob/cb72b1e9053c02a58d874ff376359a83dc3f0742/src/base/Multicall.sol) contract  which provides a  [multicall(bytes[] calldata data)](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-vultisig/blob/cb72b1e9053c02a58d874ff376359a83dc3f0742/src/base/Multicall.sol#L11) function. This function allows batching multiple function calls into a single transaction. Each subcall within `multicall` inherits the full `msg.value`, meaning that if a `payable` function like [claim( )](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-vultisig/blob/cb72b1e9053c02a58d874ff376359a83dc3f0742/src/ILOPool.sol#L184) is called multiple times within the same multicall,  it will  process the same `msg.value` each time.



 However, passing a `tokenId` which holds multiple ETH deposits by calling the [claim( )](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-vultisig/blob/cb72b1e9053c02a58d874ff376359a83dc3f0742/src/ILOPool.sol#L184) function  will use the same `msg.value` in each subcall.
 This results in multiple deposits being counted, leading to a total sum that is much larger than the actually deposited value, potentially up to the contract's entire ETH holdings , allowing an attacker to drain the contract.


## Impact
Contract holdings can be emptied as a malicious user can exploit the multicall function to repeatedly call [claim( )](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-vultisig/blob/cb72b1e9053c02a58d874ff376359a83dc3f0742/src/ILOPool.sol#L184), each time using the full `msg.value`, leading to significant over-accounting of ETH deposits and potential depletion of the contract's funds 

## Proof of Concept
The [ILOPool](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-vultisig/blob/cb72b1e9053c02a58d874ff376359a83dc3f0742/src/ILOPool.sol#) contract's [claim()](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-vultisig/blob/cb72b1e9053c02a58d874ff376359a83dc3f0742/src/ILOPool.sol#L184) function is payable and processes ETH deposits. When used within the multicall function, the same `msg.value` is reused for each subcall

An attacker can exploit this as follows : 

1. The attacker prepares a batch transaction using the multicall by calling the [claim()](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-vultisig/blob/cb72b1e9053c02a58d874ff376359a83dc3f0742/src/ILOPool.sol#L184) function with 1 ETH.
2. By calling claim 5 times in a single `multicall`, the attacker effectively gets credited with 5 ETH worth of value in exchange for 1 ETH.
3. The attacker then calls [claimRefund()](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-vultisig/blob/cb72b1e9053c02a58d874ff376359a83dc3f0742/src/ILOPool.sol#L350) to withdraw all the claims.

This results in the attacker withdrawing 5 ETH in total for the initial deposit of 1 ETH, effectively draining the contract.

## Tools Used
Manual Review
## Recommended Mitigation Steps
it is recommended to treat ETH exclusively, not allowing ETH operations to be batched at all


## Assessed type

Payable

# Lines of code

 https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-vultisig/blob/cb72b1e9053c02a58d874ff376359a83dc3f0742/src/ILOPool.sol#L368


# Vulnerability details


The [ILOPool](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-vultisig/blob/main/src/ILOPool.sol) contract allows refunding of project to the  `Manager`  by calling `claimProjectRefund(address projectAdmin)` function  which returns a call to `_refundProject(address projectAdmin)`.
 The `refundAmount` amount is computed as [refundAmount = IERC20(SALE_TOKEN).balanceOf(address(this))](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-vultisig/blob/cb72b1e9053c02a58d874ff376359a83dc3f0742/src/ILOPool.sol#L368). However , if multiple tokens with different prices are involved, simply summing their balances can result in significant discrepancies, either overpaying or underpaying the project admin

## Impact
Contract funds may be inaccurately refunded, potentially leading to significant financial discrepancies. If multiple tokens with different prices are involved, summing their balances can lead to incorrect refund amounts, resulting in either overpayment or underpayment to the project admin

## Proof of Concept
The issue arises in the following code snippet:
```solidity
function _refundProject(address projectAdmin) internal returns (uint256 refundAmount) {
@@--->   refundAmount = IERC20(SALE_TOKEN).balanceOf(address(this));
    if (refundAmount > 0) {
        TransferHelper.safeTransfer(SALE_TOKEN, projectAdmin, refundAmount);
        emit ProjectRefund(projectAdmin, refundAmount);
    }
}

```
As you can see the `balanceOf` function returns the total balance of `SALE_TOKEN` held by the contract, but it does not consider the value differences among various tokens. If multiple tokens with different prices are involved, summing their balances  can lead to incorrect refund amounts.

## Tools Used
Manual Review
## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Always consider the price differences between tokens when calculating refund amounts

Other

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-vultisig/blob/cb72b1e9053c02a58d874ff376359a83dc3f0742/src/ILOManager.sol#L33-L49
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-vultisig/blob/cb72b1e9053c02a58d874ff376359a83dc3f0742/src/ILOManager.sol#L28-L31


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
The `ILOManager` contract is deployed once (unlike `ILOPool` which is just implementation).
The contract sets the owner as the `tx.origin` in the constructor, however, a malicious user might frontrun `initialize`, which has no `ownerOnly` modifier, and can be called by anyone, to set a different admin to the contract, which might lead to unexpected results.

## Proof of Concept
The attack could unfold as follows:
1. protocol deploy the ILOManager contract.
2. the original caller will be the new owner of the contract
3. a malicious user will frontrun `initialize` function which does:
```javascript
    function initialize(
@>        address initialOwner,
        address _feeTaker,
        address iloPoolImplementation,
        address uniV3Factory,
        address weth9,
        uint16 platformFee,
        uint16 performanceFee
    ) external override whenNotInitialized {
        PLATFORM_FEE = platformFee;
        PERFORMANCE_FEE = performanceFee;
        FEE_TAKER = _feeTaker;
@>        transferOwnership(initialOwner);
        UNIV3_FACTORY = uniV3Factory;
        ILO_POOL_IMPLEMENTATION = iloPoolImplementation;
        WETH9 = weth9;
    }

```
and will take over the contract ownership.

## Tools Used
Manual review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
add `onlyOwner` modifier so only the first owner will be able to initialize the contract.


## Assessed type

Access Control

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-vultisig/blob/cb72b1e9053c02a58d874ff376359a83dc3f0742/src/ILOManager.sol#L79-L84


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
The vulnerability in the `Clones.cloneDeterministic` function within `ILOManager::initILOPool`, where the salt is generated using predictable values, poses a significant security risk. The predictability of the salt allows for frontrunning attacks, where a malicious user can use the next salt to create a contract at the same address. This can result in Denial of Service (DoS) and potential loss of funds for the protocol.

## Proof of Concept
Assume a protocol wants to create a new pool. Since the parameters used in the salt are predictable, a malicious user can use the same salt to create a contract at the same address. By using the `IILOManager` interface, they can initialize the contract with their own parameters. This can lead to two main issues:

Critical Issue: If the protocol sends tokens to this contract, a malicious user can, by using the `IILOManager` interface, initialize the contract with their own parameters, taking control of all the tokens sent to the contract. This can be especially valuable if it is not the first pool.
DoS: Since the parameters to create a pool are the same, the protocol will not be able to create any other pool in the future. The function will always revert, causing a Denial of Service.

## Tools Used
Manual review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
It is recommended to use unpredictable salts, and, when possible to include the constructor arguments withing the salt, so even if a malicious user takeover the contract, it won't be owned by someone else.


## Assessed type

DoS

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-vultisig/blob/cb72b1e9053c02a58d874ff376359a83dc3f0742/src/ILOManager.sol#L58


# Vulnerability details

## Vulnerability details
When a project is initialized using `ILOManager::initProject()`, it takes `launchTime` as param and calculates the `refundDeadline` by adding `DEFAULT_DEADLINE_OFFSET` to `launchTime`
```solidity
      uint64 refundDeadline = params.launchTime + DEFAULT_DEADLINE_OFFSET;
```
The problem is there is `no check` to ensure `launchTime` is `greater` than `block.timestamp`. As result a malicious user can pass launchTime much `earlier` than block.timestamp, which will `offset` the DEFAULT_DEADLINE_OFFSET

//How this works
1. Suppose today is sunday(9th may) and a project wanted to onboard
2. Now, instead of passing launchTime greater than 9th May, it passes date before 2nd may ie a week earlier as there is no check
3. DEFAULT_DEADLINE_OFFSET is of 7 days, as result refundDeadline = 2nd may + 7 days ie 9th may 
 
## Impact
As result, project can claimRefund() as soon as it onboarded

## Proof of Concept
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-vultisig/blob/cb72b1e9053c02a58d874ff376359a83dc3f0742/src/ILOManager.sol#L58
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-vultisig/blob/cb72b1e9053c02a58d874ff376359a83dc3f0742/src/ILOManager.sol#L202

## Tools Used
Manual Review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Add a check to ensure launchTime is greater than or equal to block.timestamp
```diff
+  require(params.launchTime >= block.timestamp, 'NA');
```

Error

# Vulnerability details

## Impact
The current implementation of the receive function uses the transfer method to return ETH to the sender. This approach forwards only 2300 gas to the recipient, which may not be sufficient for non-trivial operations in a receive or fallback function. This limitation can lead to several issues:

Inability to Receive ETH: If the sender is a contract that requires more than 2300 gas to execute its receive function, the ETH transfer will fail.
Permanent Loss of Funds: The failure of the transfer function will revert the entire transaction, preventing the sender from being whitelisted and potentially causing the sent ETH to be locked or lost if not handled properly.

## Proof of Concept
Example

Contract A is a multisig wallet or any smart contract with a receive function that consumes more than 2300 gas.
Contract A sends 1 ETH to the receive function of the target contract.
The target contract attempts to whitelist A and then return the 1 ETH using payable(msg.sender).transfer(msg.value).
Since A's receive function requires more than 2300 gas, the transfer fails, causing the entire transaction to revert.
As a result, A is not whitelisted, and the 1 ETH is not returned.

Here is the current implementation of the receive function:

```javascript
receive() external payable {
    if (_isSelfWhitelistDisabled) {
        revert SelfWhitelistDisabled();
    }
    if (_isBlacklisted[_msgSender()]) {
        revert Blacklisted();
    }
    _addWhitelistedAddress(_msgSender());
    payable(_msgSender()).transfer(msg.value); // Potential vulnerability
}
```

## Tools Used
Manual Review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
To mitigate this issue, replace the `transfer` method with `call`. The call method forwards all available gas, allowing the recipient contract to execute more complex logic in its receive function. Ensure to check the success of the call and handle failures appropriately.


## Assessed type

ETH-Transfer

# Vulnerability details

## Impact
The `_allowedWhitelistIndex` variable defines the maximum index allowed for whitelisted addresses within the contract.

```javascript
/// @notice Max index allowed
    uint256 private _allowedWhitelistIndex;
```

 Without validating this variable when adding new whitelisted addresses, several potential issues arise:

Exceeding Allowed Limits: Addresses could be added with indices that exceed `_allowedWhitelistIndex`, potentially granting unintended privileges or bypassing intended restrictions.
Contract Misconfiguration: Failure to check `_allowedWhitelistIndex` undermines the contract's intended access control mechanisms, leading to inconsistencies in whitelist management.

## Proof of Concept
Adding Addresses Without Validation:

Assume `_allowedWhitelistIndex` is set to a value restricting indices.

```javascript
/// @notice Setter for allowed whitelist index
    /// @param newIndex New index for allowed whitelist
    function setAllowedWhitelistIndex(uint256 newIndex) external onlyOwner {
        _allowedWhitelistIndex = newIndex;
    }
```

Attempt to add a new whitelisted address with an index higher than `_allowedWhitelistIndex`.
The function responsible for adding whitelisted addresses does not check `_allowedWhitelistIndex`, allowing the address to be added regardless of the allowed range.
Impact of Unchecked `_allowedWhitelistIndex`:

Addresses added without `_allowedWhitelistIndex` validation can potentially perform actions or access resources that should be restricted based on their whitelist index.
This oversight can lead to unauthorized operations or unintended access within the contract, compromising security and violating access control policies.

## Tools Used
Manual Review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
To mitigate the risk associated with the lack of validation against `_allowedWhitelistIndex` when adding whitelisted addresses, implement the following measures:

Validate `_allowedWhitelistIndex`: Ensure that before adding any address to the whitelist, the index is checked against `_allowedWhitelistIndex`.

```javascript
function addWhitelistedAddress(address whitelisted, uint256 index) external onlyOwner {
    require(index < _allowedWhitelistIndex, "Index exceeds allowed whitelist index");
    _addWhitelistedAddress(whitelisted, index);
}
```

# Vulnerability details

## Impact
The current implementation of the `checkWhitelist` function in the contract fails to enforce a cumulative check on contributions, potentially allowing addresses to `exceed` the `_maxAddressCap` limit over multiple transactions. 

_maxAddressCap exeeding the limit

Lack of cumulative checks undermines the intended control mechanisms, potentially compromising contract integrity. At the moment
Exceeding the `_maxAddressCap` could result in contractual breaches, impacting contract participants.
```javascript
if (_contributed[to] + estimatedETHAmount > _maxAddressCap) { //@udit
                revert MaxAddressCapOverflow();
            }
```

## Proof of Concept
Initial Contribution:

vultisig contributes 2 ETH to the contract, where `_maxAddressCap` is set to 3 ETH.
The function checkWhitelist validates and allows the transaction since 2 ETH is below 3 ETH.
_contributed[to] is updated to 2 ETH.
Subsequent Contributions:

3 additional transactions contributing 1 ETH each, totaling 3 more transactions.
Each time checkWhitelist is called, it checks against `_maxAddressCap` using `if (_contributed[to] + estimatedETHAmount > _maxAddressCap)`.
However,that is not properly accumulated across transactions, allowing vultsig to contribute a total of 5 ETH (2 ETH + 1 ETH + 1 ETH + 1 ETH) cumulatively, exceeding the 3 ETH cap.
Impact of Oversight:

Despite individual transactions being within the limit, cumulative contributions from repeated transactions now `exceed` `_maxAddressCap`.
The contract fails to revert transactions or enforce the cumulative limit, resulting in a breach of intended constraints.

## Tools Used
Manual Review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
To mitigate the risk associated with exceeding the `_maxAddressCap`, it is recommended to:

Implement Cumulative Contribution Tracking: Modify checkWhitelist to accumulate `_totalContributed[to]` across transactions and enforce the cumulative check against _maxAddressCap. This will make it easily to track the transaction each time some amount is added to never exeed the max.
Ensure that each transaction checks against both current and cumulative contributions to prevent unintended exceedances.

# Vulnerability details

## Impact
The absence of encoded callback data in the mint function call within the addLiquidity function can lead to unauthorized Access to Liquidity, It should contain very important values like the `poolKey`, omitting this data might allow liquidity to be added without proper payment and validation. This could result in unauthorized access to liquidity and potential financial losses for the protocol.

Without the `callback` data, the mint function may not be able to verify that the correct payment has been made, allowing an attacker to add liquidity without transferring the necessary required tokens.

## Proof of Concept
The `addLiquidity` function currently calls the mint function without passing any encoded data

```javascript
 (amount0, amount1) = params.pool.mint(
        address(this),
        TICK_LOWER,
        TICK_UPPER,
        params.liquidity,
        ""
    );
```
the mint function call includes an empty byte string ("") for the callback data,  skipping critical payment handling and verification steps.

## Tools Used
Manual Review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
update the addLiquidity function to include necessary encoded data in the mint function call. This ensures that all required operations, including payment verification and state updates, are correctly performed.

```javascript
struct MintCallbackData {
    bytes32 poolKey;
    address payer;
}
```

```javascript
 MintCallbackData memory callbackData = MintCallbackData({
        poolKey: keccak256(abi.encodePacked(address(params.pool), TICK_LOWER, TICK_UPPER)),
        payer: msg.sender
    });

    (amount0, amount1) = params.pool.mint(
        address(this),
        TICK_LOWER,
        TICK_UPPER,
        params.liquidity,
        abi.encode(callbackData)
    );
```

# Vulnerability details

## Impact
Upon analysis, the `LiquidityAmounts` library employs arithmetic operations to compute liquidity amounts from token quantities and price ranges. The library relies on imported functions such as `FullMath.mulDiv`, which are critical for accurate calculation of liquidity based on Uniswap V3 price ranges (sqrtRatioAX96 and sqrtRatioBX96).

The FullMath library was taken from Uniswap v3-core. However, the original solidity version that was used was < 0.8.0, meaning that the execution didn't revert when an overflow was reached.

## Proof of Concept
The concern arises from the potential similarity to a known vulnerability found in the FullMath library. The vulnerability in FullMath stems from its inability to handle intermediate overflows correctly, specifically in scenarios where an overflow is intended but not reached ("phantom overflow"). This oversight can lead to incorrect results or unexpected transaction reverting, particularly when precise arithmetic is pivotal for financial calculations.

***Similar Finding***
https://solodit.xyz/issues/m-10-the-fullmath-library-is-unable-to-handle-intermediate-overflows-due-to-overflow-thats-desired-but-never-reached-sherlock-uxd-uxd-protocol-git

## Tools Used
Manual review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Consider wrapping critical arithmetic operations in unchecked blocks where appropriate. This approach clarifies the intended handling of overflows, aligning with best practices to prevent unexpected reverting due to arithmetic exceptions.

Library

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-vultisig/blob/main/hardhat-vultisig/contracts/oracles/uniswap/UniswapV3Oracle.sol#L45


# Vulnerability details

## Impact

The incorrect handling of decimal scaling in the [peek function](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-vultisig/blob/main/hardhat-vultisig/contracts/oracles/uniswap/UniswapV3Oracle.sol#L39) of the UniswapV3Oracle smart contract can lead to significant errors in the calculated token prices. The function attempts to apply a 5% slippage adjustment and scale the result to the appropriate decimal precision but fails due to incorrect arithmetic operations.

This may also expose the contract to arbitrage opportunities, exploiting the discrepancy between the intended and computed token prices.

## Proof of Concept

The vulnerability results in the function returning a value that is considerably off than expected due to an excessive reduction factor (1e20 instead of 1e18), compounded by an incorrect integration of the slippage calculation. This miscomputation can lead to significant financial inaccuracies, impacting users' transactions by providing misleading financial data.

The function is designed to calculate the TWAP adjusted by a 5% slippage. However, the implementation multiplies quotedWETHAmount and baseAmount by 95 (intending a 5% reduction) and then divides by 1e20 rather than correctly applying the slippage and adjusting for token decimal places (1e18 for the tokens used). This incorrect calculation alters the output value due to the additional division by 100, which is not accounted for in the intended decimal adjustment.

Since the intention is to apply a 5% reduction and then adjust for the resulting decimal scale correctly, the division by 1e20 does both but will alter the final amount due to the additional factor of 1e2 (100 times smaller than expected).

Incorrect Implementation:
quotedWETHAmount = 1e18  # 1 ETH in wei
baseAmount = 1e18  # 1 unit of VULT in wei
result = (quotedWETHAmount * baseAmount * 95) / 1e20
`result --> 9.5e+17`

Correct Implementation:
quotedWETHAmount = 1e18  # 1 ETH in wei
baseAmount = 1e18  # 1 unit of VULT in wei
result = (quotedWETHAmount * baseAmount * 95 / 100) / 1e18
`result --> 9.499999999999999e+17`

In practice, ensuring that calculations are exact and correctly implemented as intended is vital for maintaining the expected functionality of financial applications.

## Tools Used

Manual Review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps

Modify the function to apply the 5% slippage correctly before adjusting for decimal precision:

```diff
    function peek(uint256 baseAmount) external view returns (uint256) {
        uint32 longestPeriod = OracleLibrary.getOldestObservationSecondsAgo(pool);
        uint32 period = PERIOD < longestPeriod ? PERIOD : longestPeriod;
        int24 tick = OracleLibrary.consult(pool, period);
        uint256 quotedWETHAmount = OracleLibrary.getQuoteAtTick(tick, BASE_AMOUNT, baseToken, WETH);
        // Apply 5% slippage
-        return (quotedWETHAmount * baseAmount * 95) / 1e20; // 100 / 1e18
+        return (quotedWETHAmount * baseAmount * 95 / 100) / 1e18;
    }
```


## Assessed type

Uniswap

In extra data, force as first element one that specified transaction gas limit.

# Vulnerability details

#### Summary
The LiquidityManagement contract, which inherits from PeripheryPayments, is vulnerable to disruptions caused by token blocklists (e.g., USDT) during Uniswap V3 liquidity provision. This report outlines how blocklisted addresses can impede the contract's operation in the context of adding liquidity to Uniswap V3 pools.

#### Flow of Execution
1. A user initiates the addition of liquidity through the `LiquidityManagement` contract.
2. The `addLiquidity` function of `LiquidityManagement` calls `pool.mint`, intending to deposit tokens into a Uniswap V3 pool.
3. The Uniswap V3 pool, in turn, calls the `uniswapV3MintCallback` function.
4. Within the `uniswapV3MintCallback`, the `pay` function from `PeripheryPayments` is called to transfer tokens.
5. Token transfers are attempted using the `TransferHelper.safeTransfer` or `TransferHelper.safeTransferFrom` methods.

#### Vulnerable Code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-vultisig/blob/cb72b1e9053c02a58d874ff376359a83dc3f0742/src/base/LiquidityManagement.sol#L20

function uniswapV3MintCallback(
    uint256 amount0Owed,
    uint256 amount1Owed,
    bytes calldata data
) external override {
    require(msg.sender == _cachedUniV3PoolAddress);
    if (amount0Owed > 0) pay(_cachedPoolKey.token0, address(this), msg.sender, amount0Owed);
    if (amount1Owed > 0) pay(_cachedPoolKey.token1, address(this), msg.sender, amount1Owed);
}
```
```solidity
// File: PeripheryPayments.sol
function pay(
    address token,
    address payer,
    address recipient,
    uint256 value
) internal {
    TransferHelper.safeTransferFrom(token, payer, recipient, value);
}
```

#### Proof of Concept
1. **Transaction Reverts**: When a blocklisted contract address attempts to execute `safeTransferFrom`, the transaction fails, reverting with an error if the token enforces blocklisting.
2. **Scenario Simulation**: Deploying these contracts in a test environment and simulating the addition of liquidity using a blocklisted token results in transaction failures, as predicted by the contract's logic.

#### Impact
Users attempting to provide liquidity involving blocklisted tokens experience transaction failures, leading to loss of gas fees.

#### Recommended Mitigation Steps
Before initiating token transfers, implement a function to check the blocklist status of the involved addresses

# Vulnerability details

#### Summary
The ILOPool contract's claimRefund function is prone to inaccuracies caused by external changes in token balances, such as those resulting from airdrops. These inaccuracies can lead to situations where funds are left stuck in the contract, as the calculated refund amounts may not properly account for the actual token balances.

#### Impact
Users may not be able to retrieve the full amount of their raised tokens due to discrepancies in the balance calculation, leaving funds stuck in the contract.

#### Affected Function

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-vultisig/blob/cb72b1e9053c02a58d874ff376359a83dc3f0742/src/ILOPool.sol#L350

```solidity
function claimRefund(uint256 tokenId) external override refundable() isAuthorizedForToken(tokenId) {
        uint256 refundAmount = _positions[tokenId].raiseAmount;
        address tokenOwner = ownerOf(tokenId);

        delete _positions[tokenId];
        delete _positionVests[tokenId];
        _burn(tokenId);

        TransferHelper.safeTransfer(RAISE_TOKEN, tokenOwner, refundAmount);
        emit UserRefund(tokenOwner, tokenId,refundAmount);
    }
```

This function determines the refund amount based on _positions[tokenId].raiseAmount. If the external token balance increases (e.g., due to an airdrop), the contract's accounting does not reflect this change, and users cannot claim these additional funds. Conversely, if the balance decreases (e.g., due to rebasing), users may not receive the correct amount they are entitled to, leaving excess funds in the contract.

#### Steps to Reproduce
1. Deploy the ILOPool contract and initialize it with appropriate parameters.
2. Conduct a sale, allowing users to buy positions and raise tokens.
3. Trigger an external change in the token balance (e.g., an airdrop affecting the RAISE_TOKEN).
4. Attempt to claim a refund using the claimRefund function.
5. Observe that the refund amount is incorrect and some funds remain in the contract.


The refund amounts do not account for external changes in token balances, leading to discrepancies and potentially leaving funds stuck in the contract.

#### Suggested Mitigation
Periodically sync the contract's internal accounting with the actual token balances to account for any external changes.

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-vultisig/blob/cb72b1e9053c02a58d874ff376359a83dc3f0742/hardhat-vultisig/contracts/oracles/uniswap/UniswapV3Oracle.sol#L45


# Vulnerability details


## Summary:
In the `UniswapV3Oracle` contract located at `hardhat-vultisig\contracts\oracles\uniswap\UniswapV3Oracle.sol`, there is a discrepancy between the code and the comment in the `peek` function. The comment suggests dividing by `1e18`, but the actual code divides by `1e20`. This leads to an incorrect calculation of the TWAP price for VULT/ETH, affecting the final output value significantly.

## Vulnerability Details:
The `peek` function is intended to return the TWAP (Time-Weighted Average Price) for 1 VULT for the last 30 minutes, applying a 5% slippage. The division factor used in the calculation should be `1e18` as per the comment, but the code currently uses `1e20`. This results in a substantial error in the final price calculation.

Relevant code snippet:
```solidity
return (quotedWETHAmount * baseAmount * 95) / 1e20; // 100 / 1e18
```

## Impact
The incorrect division factor leads to a hundredfold reduction in the calculated TWAP price for VULT/ETH. This can cause significant financial discrepancies and incorrect price reporting, potentially leading to substantial losses for users relying on the accurate price calculation for their transactions.

Based on the vulnerability classifications:
- **Impact**: Medium - A small amount of funds can be lost or ancillary functionality of the protocol is affected. The user or protocol may experience reduced or delayed receipt of intended funds.
- **Likelihood**: Medium - An attack vector that is only possible in uncommon cases or requires a large amount of capital to exercise relative to the amount gained or the disruption to the protocol.

Therefore, the severity of this issue is assessed as **Medium**.

## Proof of Concept
Consider the following values:
- `quotedWETHAmount = 1e18`
- `baseAmount = 1e18`

With the current code:
\[ \text{result} = \frac{1e18 \times 1e18 \times 0.95}{1e20} = 9.5 \times 10^{15} \]

With the corrected division factor (`1e18`):
\[ \text{result} = \frac{1e18 \times 1e18 \times 0.95}{1e18} = 9.5 \times 10^{17} \]

The difference is substantial and indicates a hundredfold reduction due to the incorrect division factor.

## Tools Used
- Manual Review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Update the division factor in the `peek` function to `1e18` to match the intended behavior and the comment:

```solidity
return (quotedWETHAmount * baseAmount * 95) / 1e18; // 100 / 1e18
```

This change will ensure the accurate calculation of the TWAP price for VULT/ETH, maintaining consistency between the code and the comments, and preventing potential financial discrepancies.
```

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-vultisig/blob/main/src/ILOManager.sol#L142
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-vultisig/blob/main/src/ILOManager.sol#L88-L90
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-vultisig/blob/main/src/ILOPool.sol#L72-L76
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-vultisig/blob/main/src/ILOPool.sol#L155-L159
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-vultisig/blob/main/src/ILOPool.sol#L242-L248


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
Project admins can create pools for their project by calling `ILOManager::initILOPool`, and passing in `params` argument, which specifies the initial pool values.

Once these pool values are verified, a new `ILOPool` is created for the project. The problem is that the tick values specified by the project admin are not verified correctly if it is in-range within the `initial pool price`.

The `initial pool price` is the ratio of the pool at the time the project was initialized. It is crucial that this price is within the range of the tick range specified by the caller, because the price calculations depend on it.

These price calculations include the amount of liquidity investors earn from the `raise tokens` sent and the amount of liquidity minted to the project.

A malicious project admin can manipulate these price calculations by specifying a tick range below the `initial pool price`, causing users to earn less tokens.

## Proof of Concept
When projects are initialized, the pool values are cached, including the `initialPoolPriceX96`, which represents the current ratio of the `Uniswap V3 pool`.

[ILOManager.sol#L142](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-vultisig/blob/main/src/ILOManager.sol#L142)
```javascript
_project.initialPoolPriceX96 = initialPoolPriceX96;
```

The project admin can proceed to initialize `ILOPools`, where they can specify the tick range of the pool.

[ILOManager.sol#L88-L90](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-vultisig/blob/main/src/ILOManager.sol#L88-L90)
```javascript
    uint160 sqrtRatioLowerX96 = TickMath.getSqrtRatioAtTick(params.tickLower);
    uint160 sqrtRatioUpperX96 = TickMath.getSqrtRatioAtTick(params.tickUpper);
    require(sqrtRatioLowerX96 < _project.initialPoolPriceX96 && sqrtRatioLowerX96 < sqrtRatioUpperX96, "RANGE");
```

The problem is with the check `require(sqrtRatioLowerX96 < _project.initialPoolPriceX96 && sqrtRatioLowerX96 < sqrtRatioUpperX96, "RANGE")`.

There is no verification that `_project.initialPoolPriceX96  < sqrtRatioUpperX96`. This is problematic, as it defeats the purpose of the `range` verification.

A malicious project admin can specify a `sqrtRatioUpperX96` that is far lower than `_project.initialPoolPriceX96`.

These values are initialized in the `ILOPool`, and used in calculations in `buy()`, `claim()`, `launch()` functions.

[ILOPool.sol#L72-L76](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-vultisig/blob/main/src/ILOPool.sol#L72-L76)
```javascript
    TICK_LOWER = params.tickLower;
    TICK_UPPER = params.tickUpper;
    SQRT_RATIO_LOWER_X96 = params.sqrtRatioLowerX96;
    SQRT_RATIO_UPPER_X96 = params.sqrtRatioUpperX96;
    SQRT_RATIO_X96 = _project.initialPoolPriceX96;
```

This could impact investors, who may receive less liquidity for the amount of `raise tokens` they invest:

[ILOPool.sol#L155-L159](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-vultisig/blob/main/src/ILOPool.sol#L155-L159)
```javascript
    if (RAISE_TOKEN == _cachedPoolKey.token0) {
        liquidityDelta = LiquidityAmounts.getLiquidityForAmount0(SQRT_RATIO_X96, SQRT_RATIO_UPPER_X96, raiseAmount);
    } else {
        liquidityDelta = LiquidityAmounts.getLiquidityForAmount1(SQRT_RATIO_LOWER_X96, SQRT_RATIO_X96, raiseAmount);
    }
```

Or cause users to earn less on claims

[ILOPool.sol#L242-L248](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-vultisig/blob/main/src/ILOPool.sol#L242-L248)
```javascript
    (uint128 amountCollected0, uint128 amountCollected1) = pool.collect(
        address(this),
        TICK_LOWER,
        TICK_UPPER,
        type(uint128).max,
        type(uint128).max
    );
```

## Tools Used
Manual review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Make the following changes to ensure that the prices are in-range

```diff
- require(sqrtRatioLowerX96 < _project.initialPoolPriceX96 && sqrtRatioLowerX96 < sqrtRatioUpperX96, "RANGE");
+ require(sqrtRatioLowerX96 < _project.initialPoolPriceX96 && _project.initialPoolPriceX96 < sqrtRatioUpperX96 && sqrtRatioLowerX96 < sqrtRatioUpperX96, "RANGE"); 
```


## Assessed type

Error

`ILOPool::buy` allows whitelisted recipients to invest in a project and mints an NFT of their position corresponding to liquidity amount for the amount of `raise tokens` they transferred.

`ILOPool::claim` allows users to claim tokens associated with their position ID, and returns the amounts of token0 and token1 that were collected for the position represented by the position (token) ID.

This is done by calling external `burn()` and `collect()` functions of the `Uniswap v3 pool`. The problem is the amount they receive may change prior to execution (i.e, while it's in the mempool), which can cause users to receive much less amount than they are owed.

## Proof of Concept
[ILOPool.sol#L205)](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-vultisig/blob/main/src/ILOPool.sol#L205)
```javascript
    // get amount of token0 and token1 that pool will return for us
    (amount0, amount1) = pool.burn(TICK_LOWER, TICK_UPPER, liquidity2Claim);
```

The external `Uniswap v3 pool` is called with the amount of liquidity the caller is eligible to claim, and this amount is burned. The caller is returned the amount of tokens received from the burn.

When the external burn call is executed, to calculate the amount of tokens the caller will receive, the following is executed from the `Uniswap V3 pool`

[UniswapV3Pool.sol#L336-L359](https://github.com/Uniswap/v3-core/blob/main/contracts/UniswapV3Pool.sol#L336-L359)
```javascript
    } else if (_slot0.tick < params.tickUpper) {
        // current tick is inside the passed range
        uint128 liquidityBefore = liquidity; // SLOAD for gas optimization

        // write an oracle entry
        (slot0.observationIndex, slot0.observationCardinality) = observations.write(
            _slot0.observationIndex,
            _blockTimestamp(),
            _slot0.tick,
            liquidityBefore,
            _slot0.observationCardinality,
            _slot0.observationCardinalityNext
        );

        amount0 = SqrtPriceMath.getAmount0Delta(
            _slot0.sqrtPriceX96,
            TickMath.getSqrtRatioAtTick(params.tickUpper),
            params.liquidityDelta
        );
        amount1 = SqrtPriceMath.getAmount1Delta(
            TickMath.getSqrtRatioAtTick(params.tickLower),
            _slot0.sqrtPriceX96,
            params.liquidityDelta
        );
```

These values can change prior to execution, another user may also front-run to claim before, potentially causing the caller to receive less tokens.

## Tools Used
Manual review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Incorporate slippage protection in `ILOPool::claim`


## Assessed type

Context

# Lines of code

# Vulnerability details

## Impact
Project admins can create multiple `ILOPools` for their project, which contains mechanism such as vesting, sale management, ERC721 integration, etc.

Users can earn rewards for the amount they invested by calling `ILOPool::claim()`. These rewards are calculated based off the `liquidity2claim`, which is the `amount of unlocked liquidity for the position`.

`IUniswapV3PoolActions::burn()` is called with the `liquidity2claim` amount, which burns the liquidity and returns tokens owed for the liquidity to the position, `amount0` and `amount1`, which represent the `RAISE_TOKEN` and `SALE_TOKEN`.

From the fees generated by the position, the `performanceFee` is deducted, and sent to the `feeTaker`.

When calculating how much `performanceFee` to deduct, the protocol utilizes `IUniswapV3PoolState::positions` to get the amount of fees earned from the `burn()` call.

The problem is the amount of fees collected is multiplied by the entire amount of liquidity of the position, rather than the liquidity that was claimed. This will give a greater fee value that is given to both the caller and the fee taker, which will take extra tokens from the pool, and may DoS due to insufficient tokens in some cases.

## Proof of Concept
[ILOPool.sol#L194-L195](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-vultisig/blob/main/src/ILOPool.sol#L194-L195)
```javascript
    // calculate amount of unlocked liquidity for the position
    uint128 liquidity2Claim = _claimableLiquidity(tokenId);
```

This amount of liquidity is burned from the `Uniswap V3 pool` and returns the amount of tokens owed from the amount burned.

[ILOPool.sol#L204-L205](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-vultisig/blob/main/src/ILOPool.sol#L204-L205)
```javascript
    // get amount of token0 and token1 that pool will return for us
    (amount0, amount1) = pool.burn(TICK_LOWER, TICK_UPPER, liquidity2Claim);
```

The function proceeds to calculate the fees owed to the `feeTaker`.

[ILOPool.sol#L212-L227)](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-vultisig/blob/main/src/ILOPool.sol#L212-L227)
```javascript
    // calculate amount of fees that position generated
    (, uint256 feeGrowthInside0LastX128, uint256 feeGrowthInside1LastX128, , ) = pool.positions(positionKey);
    uint256 fees0 = FullMath.mulDiv(
                        feeGrowthInside0LastX128 - position.feeGrowthInside0LastX128,
                        positionLiquidity, //@audit should be liquidity2Claim
                        FixedPoint128.Q128
                    );
    
    uint256 fees1 = FullMath.mulDiv(
                        feeGrowthInside1LastX128 - position.feeGrowthInside1LastX128,
                        positionLiquidity, //@audit should be liquidity2Claim
                        FixedPoint128.Q128
                    );

    // amount of fees after deduct performance fee
    (fees0, fees1) = _deductFees(fees0, fees1, _project.performanceFee);
```

The problem is that the entire `positionLiquidity` is used to calculate `fees0` and `fees1`, rather than `liquidity2claim`. This is problematic, as the fees earned from `burn()` are calculated from the `liquidity2Claim`, so the fees calculate are overvalued in most cases, as `positionLiquidity >= liquidity2Claim`.

[ILOPool.sol#L201-L202](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-vultisig/blob/main/src/ILOPool.sol#L201-L202)
```javascript
    uint128 positionLiquidity = position.liquidity;
    require(positionLiquidity >= liquidity2Claim);
```

These fees are added to the amount to send to the user, and will send a portion of it to the `feeTaker`.

Since the token amounts are over-valued, this may DoS due to insufficient tokens, or users will lose funds as more pool tokens will be lost.

## Tools Used
Manual review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Make the following changes when calculating the fee owed

```diff
    uint256 fees0 = FullMath.mulDiv(
                        feeGrowthInside0LastX128 - position.feeGrowthInside0LastX128,
-                       positionLiquidity,
+                       liquidity2Claim
                        FixedPoint128.Q128
                    );
    
    uint256 fees1 = FullMath.mulDiv(
                        feeGrowthInside1LastX128 - position.feeGrowthInside1LastX128,
-                       positionLiquidity,
+                       liquidity2Claim
                        FixedPoint128.Q128
                    );
```

# Vulnerability details

## Impact
In the contest [README](https://code4rena.com/audits/2024-06-vultisig#top:~:text=ERC20%20token%20behaviors%20in%20scope), the protocol mentions that `ERC20 Missing return values` are in-scope.

One of these ERC20 tokens is USDT, which does not return type `bool` on mainnet. The protocol utilizes `TransferHelper` with openzeppelin's `IERC20` functions for `transfer` and `approval`. These functions return type `bool`, thus the function signature will not match with `USDT`, and will revert.

Projects will not be compatible with `USDT`.

## Proof of Concept
[ILOPool.sol#L251-L260](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-vultisig/blob/main/src/ILOPool.sol#L251-L260)
```javascript
    // transfer token for user
    TransferHelper.safeTransfer(_cachedPoolKey.token0, ownerOf(tokenId), amount0);
    TransferHelper.safeTransfer(_cachedPoolKey.token1, ownerOf(tokenId), amount1);

    emit Claim(ownerOf(tokenId), tokenId,liquidity2Claim, amount0, amount1, position.feeGrowthInside0LastX128, position.feeGrowthInside1LastX128);

    address feeTaker = IILOManager(MANAGER).FEE_TAKER();
    // transfer fee to fee taker
    TransferHelper.safeTransfer(_cachedPoolKey.token0, feeTaker, amountCollected0-amount0);
    TransferHelper.safeTransfer(_cachedPoolKey.token1, feeTaker, amountCollected1-amount1);
```

Protocol utilizes `TransferHelper` library for tokens transfers and approval.

[TransferHelper.sol#L20](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-vultisig/blob/main/src/libraries/TransferHelper.sol#L20)
```javascript
token.call(abi.encodeWithSelector(IERC20.transferFrom.selector, from, to, value));
```

Openzeppelin's `IERC20.transferFrom` function selector is used.

[IERC20.sol#L26](https://github.com/OpenZeppelin/openzeppelin-contracts/blob/04695aecbd4d17dddfd55de766d10e3805d6f42f/contracts/token/ERC20/IERC20.sol#L26)
```javascript
  function transfer(address recipient, uint256 amount) external returns (bool);
```

We can see it returns a bool. The same applies to `transferFrom` and `approve`.

USDT on mainnet does not return a bool, as you can see [here](https://etherscan.io/token/0xdac17f958d2ee523a2206206994597c13d831ec7#code).

The function signatures will not match, and therefore the call will revert.

## Tools Used
Manual review.

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Use openzeppelin's [SafeERC20](https://github.com/OpenZeppelin/openzeppelin-contracts/blob/master/contracts/token/ERC20/utils/SafeERC20.sol)


## Assessed type

ERC20

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-vultisig/blob/cb72b1e9053c02a58d874ff376359a83dc3f0742/hardhat-vultisig/contracts/oracles/uniswap/uniswapv0.8/FullMath.sol#L83


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
Detailed description of the impact of this finding.

Using the bitwise XOR operator instead of the exponential operator results in incorrect calculations, which can lead to severe financial discrepancies and security vulnerabilities within the smart contract. Incorrect values can propagate through the contract, leading to unintended behaviors, loss of funds, or manipulation by malicious actors.

A vulnerability has been found in the FullMath.sol contract located at https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-vultisig/blob/cb72b1e9053c02a58d874ff376359a83dc3f0742/hardhat-vultisig/contracts/oracles/uniswap/uniswapv0.8/FullMath.sol#L83. The vulnerability arises from the incorrect usage of the bitwise XOR operator (^) instead of the exponential operator (**).

Location: FullMath.sol, line 83
Vulnerable Formula: uint256 inv = (3 * denominator) ^ 2;

The incorrect usage of the bitwise XOR operator can lead to erroneous calculations, which may affect the correctness and security of the contract.

## Proof of Concept
Provide direct links to all referenced code in GitHub. Add screenshots, logs, or any other relevant proof that illustrates the concept.

A simple proof of concept is provided to demonstrate the incorrect calculation using the bitwise XOR operator.

Prerequisites:
1. Create foundry test file with the code below here: test/FullMath.t.sol

```sol
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
pragma solidity >=0.7.6;
pragma abicoder v2;

import "forge-std/Test.sol";
import {FullMath} from "../hardhat-vultisig/contracts/oracles/uniswap/uniswapv0.8/FullMath.sol";

contract FullMathTest is Test {

      function testFailExpoBitwiseXOR() public {
       uint256 denominator = uint256(5);

       uint256 inv = (3 * denominator) ^ 2; 
       uint256 inv2 = (3 * denominator) ** 2;

       assertEq(inv, inv2, "These should match. ");

      }
}
```

2. Go to terminal>> change directory to root folder: 2024-06-vultisig
3. Run: forge test -vvvvv --match-contract FullMathTest

```bash
forge test -vvvvv --match-contract FullMathTest
[⠊] Compiling...
[⠘] Compiling 1 files with Solc 0.7.6
[⠃] Solc 0.7.6 finished in 682.30ms
Compiler run successful with warnings:
Warning (2018): Function state mutability can be restricted to pure
test/FullMath.t.sol:10:7: Warning: Function state mutability can be restricted to pure
      function testFailExpoBitwiseXOR() public {
      ^ (Relevant source part starts here and spans across multiple lines).

Ran 1 test for test/FullMath.t.sol:FullMathTest
[PASS] testFailExpoBitwiseXOR() (gas: 2279)
Traces:
  [2279] FullMathTest::testFailExpoBitwiseXOR()
    ├─ [0] VM::assertEq(13, 225, "These should match. ") [staticcall]
    │   └─ ← [Revert] These should match. : 13 != 225
    └─ ← [Revert] These should match. : 13 != 225

Suite result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed; 0 skipped; finished in 1.08ms (241.54µs CPU time)

Ran 1 test suite in 123.56ms (1.08ms CPU time): 1 tests passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped (1 total tests)
```
## Tools Used
Manual review and Foundry Test POC.
## Recommended Mitigation Steps
The formula should use the exponential operator to ensure correct calculations.

Bad:
```sol
        uint256 inv = (3 * denominator) ^ 2;
```
Good
```sol
        uint256 inv = (3 * denominator) ** 2;
```

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-vultisig/blob/main/src/ILOManager.sol#L57-L65
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-vultisig/blob/main/src/ILOManager.sol#L124-L147


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
By IloManager design every new Project bounded to unique Uniswap V3 Pool(and vice versa) and only admin of such project can use this V3 Pool to create his own IloPools. 
Because of vulnerability it's possible to cause DoS attack by front-running new projects creation and acquire admin roles. 

Because amount of [Fee tiers](https://support.uniswap.org/hc/en-us/articles/20904283758349-What-are-fee-tiers) for V3 Pools is about four this vector of attack can be done without any extra steps to block all Pools for current pair.

## Proof of Concept
1) Project created with **initProject()** by User.
2) Attacker front-run transaction with similar params(to get same V3 Pool address)
```
        PoolAddress.PoolKey memory poolKey = PoolAddress.getPoolKey(params.saleToken, params.raiseToken, params.fee);
        uniV3PoolAddress = _initUniV3PoolIfNecessary(poolKey, params.initialPoolPriceX96);
```
3) Project and Pool created, Attacker becomes and admin of the project.
4) User's transaction get reverted because Project already exists by this V3 Pool address.
```
        Project storage _project = _cachedProject[uniV3PoolAddress];
        require(_project.uniV3PoolAddress == address(0), "RE");
```
5) All future **initProject()** calls with same saleToken,  raiseToken, fee and initialPoolPriceX96 will be blocked.

## Tools Used
Manual

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Because concept of unique V3 Pool per Project is a main design concept, there two ways how to mitigate:
1) Create an option for Owner to cleanup blocked **_cachedProject[]** from malicious projects. 
2) Introduce Whitelist for IloManager.





## Assessed type

DoS

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-vultisig/blob/main/src/ILOPool.sol#L221


# Vulnerability details

## Impact

In the `ILOPool:claim` function, there is no check to verify if `feeGrowthInside0LastX128` is zero. If it is zero, this subtraction can cause an underflow.

## Proof of Concept

Scenario:
1. A user attempts to claim.
2. `feeGrowthInside0LastX128` is less than `position.feeGrowthInside0LastX128`.
3. The value underflows and becomes the maximum value of `uint256`.
4. The code attempts to multiply `uint256` max with `positionLiquidity`.
5. This results in an overflow, producing incorrect results.

## Tools Used

Manual Review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps

Add checks to ensure `feeGrowthInside0LastX128` is greater than `position.feeGrowthInside0LastX128` to prevent underflow. Similarly, add a check for `feeGrowthInside1LastX128`.

```javascript
require(feeGrowthInside0LastX128 > position.feeGrowthInside0LastX128, "error");
require(feeGrowthInside1LastX128 > position.feeGrowthInside1LastX128, "error");
```

This ensures that the subtraction will not cause an underflow, thus maintaining the integrity of the calculations.


## Assessed type

Under/Overflow

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-vultisig/blob/main/hardhat-vultisig/contracts/Whitelist.sol#L216-L218


# Vulnerability details

`Whitelist.sol: checkWhitelist()` is intended to check if a buyer is eligible for token transfers. However even if a user is not whitelisted he will still pass the whitelist check in this function.

## Impact
Possibly loss of funds for the protocol. Because `checkWhitelist()` is used in the `_beforeTokenTransfer` hook this means that non-whitelisted users will still be able to get token transfers.

## Proof of Concept
Here is the problematic if statement in `checkWhitelist()`:
```solidity
            if (_allowedWhitelistIndex == 0 || _whitelistIndex[to] > _allowedWhitelistIndex) {
                revert NotWhitelisted();
            }
```
The index for every whitelisted user is stored in the `_whitelistIndex` mapping. `_allowedWhitelistIndex` is used to determine how many users are allowed to be whitelisted. For example if the mapping contains indexes of 10 users but `_allowedWhitelistIndex` is 5 then only the first 5 whitelisted users are eligible. That's why we are comparing them.

The issue is that if the `to` address is not whitelisted the mapping will return zero and the check `_whitelistIndex[to] > _allowedWhitelistIndex` will be false and it will not revert like it should.

## Tools Used
Manual Review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Check if `_whitelistIndex` mapping returns zero. This check should be sufficient because whitelisted user indexes start from 1 not 0.

```diff
-           if (_allowedWhitelistIndex == 0 || _whitelistIndex[to] > _allowedWhitelistIndex) {
+           if (_allowedWhitelistIndex == 0 || _whitelistIndex[to] == 0 || _whitelistIndex[to] > _allowedWhitelistIndex) {
                revert NotWhitelisted();
            }
```


## Assessed type

Other

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-vultisig/blob/main/hardhat-vultisig/contracts/oracles/uniswap/uniswapv0.8/FullMath.sol#L2
https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-vultisig/blob/main/hardhat-vultisig/contracts/oracles/uniswap/uniswapv0.8/TickMath.sol#L2


# Vulnerability details

The `TickMath.sol` and `FullMath.sol` libraries were taken from Uniswap. However Uniswap implements them with solidity version `< 0.8.0`. This solidity version introduces overflow and underflow protection. Which means operations will revert if they lead to overflow/underflow. 

The issue is that the version upper cap has been removed in this protocol's implementation but the arithmetic operations are not be wrapped in an unchecked block.

## Impact
`TickMath.sol:getSqrtRatioAtTick()` is used to get the upper/lower sqrtRatioX96 in `ILOManager.sol`:
```solidity
        uint160 sqrtRatioLowerX96 = TickMath.getSqrtRatioAtTick(params.tickLower);
        uint160 sqrtRatioUpperX96 = TickMath.getSqrtRatioAtTick(params.tickUpper);
```
`FullMath.sol: mulDiv()` is used multiple times in `ILOPool.sol`.

## Proof of Concept
`getSqrtRatioAtTick()` will not behave as intended since it relies implicitly on overflows.

In `mulDiv()` when a phantom overflow (a multiplication and division where an intermediate value overflows 256 bits) occurs the execution will revert and the correct result won't be returned.

This issue has also been addressed by Spearbit as a High/Medium severity:
[Issue 1](https://solodit.xyz/issues/use-unchecked-intickmathsol-andfullmathsol-spearbit-overlay-pdf)
[Issue 2](https://solodit.xyz/issues/tickmath-might-revert-in-solidity-version-08-spearbit-timeless-pdf)
[Issue 3](https://solodit.xyz/issues/fullmath-requires-overflow-behavior-spearbit-morpho-pdf)

## Tools Used
Manual Review

## Recommended Mitigation Steps
Use the modified version of the original `TickMath.sol` and `FullMath.sol` for version `^0.8.0` that can be found [here](https://github.com/Uniswap/v3-core/tree/0.8/contracts/libraries). These implementations wrap the arithmetic operations in an `unchecked` block to handle the overflow.


## Assessed type

Other

# Lines of code

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-vultisig/blob/cb72b1e9053c02a58d874ff376359a83dc3f0742/hardhat-vultisig/contracts/oracles/uniswap/UniswapV3Oracle.sol#L45

https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-vultisig/blob/cb72b1e9053c02a58d874ff376359a83dc3f0742/hardhat-vultisig/contracts/oracles/uniswap/UniswapV3Oracle.sol#L45


# Vulnerability details

## Impact
`UniswapV3Oracle:peek` has a bug in the calculation of the returned value in the following line: [UniswapV3Oracle.sol#L45](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-vultisig/blob/cb72b1e9053c02a58d874ff376359a83dc3f0742/hardhat-vultisig/contracts/oracles/uniswap/UniswapV3Oracle.sol#L45)
```solidity
return (quotedWETHAmount * baseAmount * 95) / 1e20; // 100 / 1e18
```
The comment suggests that a 5% slippage will be applied to the quoted WETH amount. However, the calculation is incorrect.

This should be corrected to:
```solidity
return (quotedWETHAmount * baseAmount * 95) / 100 / 1e18;
```
**Explanation**
   - `quotedWETHAmount` represents the quoted WETH amount for 1 VULT (1e18 base amount).
   - `baseAmount` is the input amount of VULT for which the price is being calculated.
   - To apply a 5% slippage, the quoted WETH amount should be multiplied by 0.95 (95% of the original amount).
   - The division by `1e20` in the original code is incorrect. It should be a division by `100` to convert the percentage to a decimal, followed by a division by `1e18` to adjust for the decimals of VULT.

**So, the corrected calculation should be**
   1. Multiply `quotedWETHAmount` by `baseAmount` to get the total WETH amount for the given `baseAmount` of VULT.
   2. Multiply the result by 95 to apply the 5% slippage.
   3. Divide the result by 100 to convert the percentage to a decimal.
   4. Divide the result by 1e18 to adjust for the decimals of VULT.

This will give the correct WETH amount with a 5% slippage applied.

## Proof of Concept
[UniswapV3Oracle.sol#L38-L46](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-vultisig/blob/cb72b1e9053c02a58d874ff376359a83dc3f0742/hardhat-vultisig/contracts/oracles/uniswap/UniswapV3Oracle.sol#L38-L46)
```solidity
function peek(uint256 baseAmount) external view returns (uint256) {
    uint32 longestPeriod = OracleLibrary.getOldestObservationSecondsAgo(pool);
    uint32 period = PERIOD < longestPeriod ? PERIOD : longestPeriod;
    int24 tick = OracleLibrary.consult(pool, period);
    uint256 quotedWETHAmount = OracleLibrary.getQuoteAtTick(tick, BASE_AMOUNT, baseToken, WETH);
    // Apply 5% slippage
    return (quotedWETHAmount * baseAmount * 95) / 1e20; // 100 / 1e18
}
```
The incorrect calculation [UniswapV3Oracle.sol#L46](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-vultisig/blob/cb72b1e9053c02a58d874ff376359a83dc3f0742/hardhat-vultisig/contracts/oracles/uniswap/UniswapV3Oracle.sol#L45)
```solidity
return (quotedWETHAmount * baseAmount * 95) / 1e20; // 100 / 1e18
```

   - Suppose `quotedWETHAmount` is 0.01 WETH (10000000000000000 wei) for 1 VULT (1e18 base amount).
   - If `baseAmount` is 2e18 (2 VULT), the expected result with a 5% slippage would be 0.019 WETH (19000000000000000 wei).
With the incorrect calculation:

With the incorrect calculation
```solidity
(10000000000000000 * 2e18 * 95) / 1e20
= 1900000000000000000000 / 1e20
= 19 wei
```
With the corrected calculation
```solidity
(10000000000000000 * 2e18 * 95) / 100 / 1e18
= 1900000000000000000000 / 100 / 1e18
= 19000000000000000 wei
```
As you can see, the incorrect calculation results in a significantly undervalued amount (19 wei instead of 0.019 WETH), while the corrected calculation provides the expected result.

```solidity
quoteAmount = baseToken < quoteToken
    ? FullMath.mulDiv(ratioX192, baseAmount, 1 << 192)
    : FullMath.mulDiv(1 << 192, baseAmount, ratioX192);
```
and
[OracleLibrary.sol#L52-L54](https://github.com/code-423n4/2024-06-vultisig/blob/cb72b1e9053c02a58d874ff376359a83dc3f0742/hardhat-vultisig/contracts/oracles/uniswap/uniswapv0.8/OracleLibrary.sol#L52-L54)
```solidity
quoteAmount = baseToken < quoteToken
    ? FullMath.mulDiv(ratioX128, baseAmount, 1 << 128)
    : FullMath.mulDiv(1 << 128, baseAmount, ratioX128);
```
